newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Nippecraft may be target of takeover.
newsitem.headline: Nippecraft may be target of takeover.

text.p: Stationary maker Nippecraft said on Thursday it expects to incur a loss of Singapore $11.9 million for the current financial year ending March 31 and could be a target of a takeover.
It said in a statement it was awaiting an annoucement from major shareholder St Kilda Investments, currently in talks with an investor for a sale of its 64 percent stake in Nippecraft.
Nippecraft asked the Stock Exchange of Singapore to suspend trade in its shares on February 24.
"They expect to come out with an announcement as soon as possible, the 28th (of February) at the latest," company secretary Tan Sing Yuen said.
Nippecraft directors said the expected loss of $11.9 million would be on a consolidated turnover of about $64 million for the current financial year ending March 31, 1997.
The loss includes a further $1.2 million write-off of obsolete stocks which may have to be provided for.
But the directors said that barring unforseen circumstances, they expected better prospects for the next financial year.
The company will make inroads into the German and Japanese markets while continuing to intensify efforts in North America. It will also explore untapped markets in Asia, it said.
Nippecraft turned in a first-half loss of $4.6 million for the six months to September 30, against profits of $1.1 million in the previous six months.
